svg.title: Match the phenotype categories to their model
svg.desc: Three expression models are compared. Complete dominance maps AA and Aa to one phenotype and aa to another, yielding3:1 phenotypes from Aa×Aa. In the fictional incomplete-dominance flower model, RᴿRᴿ is red, RᴿRᵂ pink and RᵂRᵂ white; two pink parents produce these at1/4,1/2,1/4. Genotype and phenotype ratios are1:2:1 because the heterozygote is separately scored. The alleles remain distinct and segregate rather than blending irreversibly. Codominance means both allele-associated products are detectable in a heterozygote, not an intermediate blended product. Dominance relationships depend on the chosen measurement and mechanism.

g.text: Match the phenotype categories to their model
The same segregation principle can produce different scored phenotype patterns.
AA → dominant; Aa → dominant; aa → recessive
RᴿRᴿ → red; RᴿRᵂ → pink; RᵂRᵂ → white
Pink × pink: ¼ red, ½ pink, ¼ white; both ratios 1:2:1.
A heterozygote displays both allele-associated products.
Both products are detected; neither is an intermediate blended product.
State notation and what is measured before selecting the model or calculating.
An intermediate phenotype does not destroy the separate alleles; red and white can reappear.
